description: Three small tables on Bahrain's open data portal, from the Information and eGovernment Authority, give the housing units counted in the 2020 census. One splits units by type (flat, villa, conventional house, traditional house and others) and by whether they were occupied or vacant: for example 122,048 flats were occupied and 91,403 vacant, and 96,142 villas occupied and 30,779 vacant. The second gives housing units by type for each of the four governorates, and the third counts occupied housing units by the number of cars in each governorate. Coverage is the whole Kingdom at governorate level; labels are in English and Arabic, and the metadata was last modified on 6 June 2023. The same portal holds some 45 Census 2020 tables in all, most on population. Format and access: view, export and query through the Opendatasoft explore API, free and without registration. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): Bahrain Government Open Data License. Caveats: governorate level only, a handful of rows per table, and no service or building age variables. Simulation uses: vacancy and dwelling mix for housing and utility demand, and car ownership by governorate for transport demand. Related records: the Bahrain Census 2020 buildings tables, which come from the same portal.
